title: Post Mint Deduplication
definition: The process of eliminating duplicate concepts from a list of concepts, typically after they have been minted but before they are saved.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine you're collecting stickers and you accidentally get some duplicates. Post-mint deduplication is like checking your collection to make sure there are no repeats before you display it.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Post-mint deduplication involves running a function on a list of concepts after they've been extracted from a source but before they're saved or reviewed. This function removes any duplicate concepts, ensuring data integrity.
difficulty_levels.expert: Post-mint deduplication is a critical step in data processing to ensure the accuracy and efficiency of a system. By eliminating duplicates from a list of concepts, the system can save storage space, improve performance, and avoid inconsistencies. Furthermore, the timing of this process — just before review and minting — allows for the greatest level of control and flexibility, as it ensures that the deduplicated data is used in all subsequent steps without affecting earlier stages of the pipeline.

extra_fields.insight: The importance of post-mint deduplication as a critical step in data processing and its implications for data integrity and system performance.
